title: Disclosure notice, an explicit wallet fact, then a constrained shortlist
notice: Synthetic and illustrative. Card names, facts, identifiers and field names are invented for this example. The live server's advertised schemas are authoritative.
demonstrates: The assistant explains what is saved, including request history, before the first Rewardopedia call.
Only an explicit statement becomes a wallet fact.
A clearly named goal is mapped to its goal token, and the assistant says which goal it used.
A card whose fee is unknown does not pass a fee constraint.
Conditions and limitations stay attached to each candidate.

steps.text: I already have the Example Cash Card. Dining is my priority and I don't want an annual fee over $95.

Before I use Rewardopedia: it keeps a sanitized history of each Rewardopedia request in your Rewardopedia account until you delete it, and it saves facts you tell me, such as the cards you hold and your goals and constraints, unless you ask me not to. Both are shared across assistants connected to your account, and you can ask what is saved or ask me to forget it at any time. Please don't share card or account numbers. Shall I save that you hold the Example Cash Card, that your goal is dining, and that your annual fee limit is $95?

candidates.name: Example Dining Card
reasons: Earns 3x Example Points on dining, capped at $6,000 of dining spend per year; 1x after the cap.
limitations: Example Points are not cash; their value depends on how they are redeemed.

steps.text: One card fits your dining goal and $95 limit: the Example Dining Card. It earns 3x Example Points on dining, but only on the first $6,000 of dining spend each year (1x after that), and its annual fee is $95. Example Points are not cash, so their value depends on how you redeem them. The Example Premium Card was not included because its annual fee is unknown, so it cannot be shown to meet your limit. Source: issuer.example.
